description: Assemble or modify electrical or electronic equipment, such as computers, test equipment telemetering systems, electric motors, and batteries.

onet_30_3.name: O*NET 30.3 Database
onet_30_3.methodology: O*NET 30.3 Database by the U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration (USDOL/ETA), used under the CC BY 4.0 license. This dataset modifies the original: 8-digit O*NET-SOC specialties are rolled up to 6-digit 2018 SOC codes, skill/knowledge importances are the maximum across constituent specialties, and related-occupation tiers are converted to numeric edge weights. Every qualifying 8-digit specialty occupation (a description plus at least one of own skill ratings, technology skills, or related occupations — no family cap since v3.2.0) is additionally promoted to a first-class entry with its own O*NET description, skills, technology list, and related occupations; each promoted specialty is linked to a wage-parent occupation from which it inherits wage, employment, and projection figures (BLS publishes no specialty-level estimates) — normally its 6-digit parent, or, where OEWS folds the parent into a combined aggregate line (e.g. 29-2010), that aggregate line.

oews_may2025.name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics
oews_may2025.methodology: National cross-industry employment and annual wage percentile estimates. Wages reported by BLS as unavailable are null (suppressed); wages at or above $239,200 are top-coded by BLS and reported here as null with status "top_coded".

ep_2024_34.name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Projections
ep_2024_34.methodology: Employment Projections program, 2024–34 National Employment Matrix (occupation.xlsx Table 1.2: projected employment, percent change, annual average openings; education.xlsx Table 5.4: typical entry-level education, related work experience, and on-the-job training).

skill_similarity.name: Skill-similarity edges (computed)
skill_similarity.methodology: Derived edge layer (kind: "skill") computed by this pipeline — these are NOT published O*NET relationships. For each occupation, a vector over all O*NET Skills and Knowledge elements (importance ratings 1–5, missing elements treated as 0) is L2-normalized; cosine similarity is computed for every in-graph pair not already connected by an O*NET related-occupations edge. Pairs with similarity >= 0.98 qualify, and each occupation keeps at most its 3 strongest skill edges (greedy, strongest similarity first). Edge weight = 0.15 + (sim − 0.98)/(1 − 0.98) × 0.45, i.e. bounded to [0.15, 0.6] — always weaker than strong related-occupation edges.

layout.name: CareerGraph precomputed layout
layout.methodology: Deterministic 3D force-directed layout (d3-force-3d with a seeded mulberry32 PRNG): link distance inversely proportional to O*NET relatedness weight, many-body repulsion, collision radius proportional to the cube root of employment, and per-SOC-major-group cluster anchors arranged on a circle in the XZ plane. Computed skill-similarity edges participate as link forces at reduced strength (×0.4) so they bridge clusters without collapsing them. After free relaxation, the vertical (y) axis is fixed to normalized log median annual wage, so height encodes pay.

onet_interests.name: O*NET 30.3 Database — Occupational Interests (RIASEC)
onet_interests.methodology: O*NET 30.3 per-occupation Occupational Interest ratings (Career Interest Types file; elements 1.B.1.a Realistic … 1.B.1.f Conventional, scale OI 1–7) by USDOL/ETA, used under the CC BY 4.0 license. Scores are rescaled to 0–100 integers as round(((OI − 1) / 6) × 100) and reported in R, I, A, S, E, C order. 8-digit specialty occupations without their own ratings carry the parent occupation's profile (noted per metric); occupations with no Interests row omit the field entirely — never estimated.

onet_work_context.name: O*NET 30.3 Database — Work Context
onet_work_context.methodology: O*NET 30.3 Work Context ratings by USDOL/ETA, used under the CC BY 4.0 license. Context means (CX scale, 1–5) are rescaled to 0–100 as round(((CX − 1) / 4) × 100); categorical means (CT scale, 1–3) as round(((CT − 1) / 2) × 100). The five work-life dimensions are COMPUTED by this pipeline from those rescaled items: outdoors = max(Outdoors Exposed to All Weather Conditions [4.C.2.a.1.c], 0.5 × Outdoors Under Cover [4.C.2.a.1.d]); physical = mean(Spend Time Standing [4.C.2.d.1.b], Spend Time Walking or Running [4.C.2.d.1.d], Spend Time Bending or Twisting Your Body [4.C.2.d.1.h]); irregular = 0.5 × (100 − percent reporting a Regular schedule [4.C.3.d.4, CTP category 1; the CT mean rescaled is used for the few occupations without published category percents]) + 0.5 × Duration of Typical Work Week [4.C.3.d.8, CT]; hazard = max(Exposed to Hazardous Conditions [4.C.2.c.1.d], Exposed to Hazardous Equipment [4.C.2.c.1.e], 0.5 × Exposed to Disease or Infections [4.C.2.c.1.b]). remote is a DERIVED feasibility proxy, not a surveyed figure: remote = clamp(0.6 × (100 − Physical Proximity [4.C.2.a.3]) + 0.4 × E-Mail use [4.C.1.a.2.h], 0–100) — low physical proximity plus high computer-mediated communication; it appears as item id "derived.remote" and the UI must label it computed. 8-digit specialties without own Work Context rows carry the parent occupation's ratings (noted per item); occupations with no rows omit the fields — never estimated.

oews_history.name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (historical national)
oews_history.methodology: Annual median wage (A_MEDIAN) per SOC from the national OEWS files for May 2015 through May 2025. May 2021 onward uses the 2018 SOC, matching this dataset's codes; May 2015–2018 use the 2010 SOC and May 2019–2020 a hybrid vintage, so a pre-2021 point is included ONLY when the identical code string exists in that year's file AND its title then, normalized, matches the current title — codes that changed meaning in the 2018 SOC revision have their earlier years excluded and carry an explanatory note. Suppressed ("*") and top-coded ("#") medians are null with status, never estimated. 8-digit specialties inherit the parent occupation's series (BLS publishes no specialty-level history).

bls_cpi_u.name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U)
bls_cpi_u.methodology: CPI-U, U.S. city average, all items (series CUUR0000SA0), annual averages (LABSTAT period M13). Used to restate historical medians in May-2025 dollars — a DERIVED figure: real2025 = round(nominal × CPI-U(2025) / CPI-U(year)); the 2025 point equals its nominal value. The UI must label the adjustment as computed.

onet_constituents.name: O*NET 30.3 Database — constituent occupations of combined OEWS lines
onet_constituents.methodology: This is an OEWS-only combined line: BLS publishes employment and wages for "Electrical, Electronic, and Electromechanical Assemblers, Except Coil Winders, Tapers, and Finishers" (51-2028) as one occupation, while O*NET models its constituents separately: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers (51-2022); Electromechanical Equipment Assemblers (51-2023). Wage/employment figures are the combined line's own BLS estimates. The description is the dominant constituent's O*NET description. Skill/knowledge/technology ratings, the importance vector, interests, work context, and job zone are those O*NET publishes for Electrical and Electronic Equipment Assemblers (51-2022) — chosen because it is the dominant by employment: 82.8% of the constituents' combined 264,070 jobs in May 2016 (last OEWS year publishing them separately); ratings are NEVER averaged across occupations. Related careers are the union of all constituents' O*NET related occupations.
